                                     PROJECT NO. 58000
RULEMAKING TO UPDATE WHOLESALE                            §   PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
AND IOU RETAIL TRANSMISSION COST                          §   COMMISSION
RECOVERY IN THE ERCOT REGION                              §   OF TEXAS



                   COMMENTS OF HUNT ENERGY NETWORK, LLC

Hunt Energy Network, LLC (“Hunt Energy Network”) respectfully submits these comments in
response to the Public Utility Commission of Texas’ (“Commission”) Proposal for Publication of
amendments to 16 Texas Administrative Code (“TAC”) §§ 25.192 and 25.193 and new § 25.252,
filed in the above-referenced project on July 10, 2026.

At the outset, Hunt Energy Network thanks Commission Staff for its considerable effort in
developing this proposal to implement Section 6 of Senate Bill 6. The proposed rules reflect a
thoughtful and well-organized approach to a complex set of issues, and Hunt Energy Network
appreciates the opportunity to participate. Our comments are limited and offered in the spirit of a
technical clean-up: we identify a single provision that, as currently worded, may be read more
broadly than we believe Staff intended, and we propose a narrow clarifying edit to address it.

Proposed Clarification to § 25.192(e)(6)
Proposed § 25.192(e)(6) provides:

       “(6) Notwithstanding any other provision of this section, transmission
       interconnection costs associated with interconnection agreements signed after the
       effective date of this section must not be included in a TSP’s transmission cost of
       service or transmission service rates.”

The operative phrase — “interconnection agreements” — is unqualified. Read in isolation, it could
be understood to reach any interconnection agreement, including a Standard Generation
Interconnection Agreement (“SGIA”) executed under § 25.195 of this title (relating to Terms and
Conditions for Transmission Service). Hunt Energy Network does not believe that reading reflects
Staff’s intent, but we think the ambiguity is worth curing before adoption.

The concern is concrete. As the Commission recently confirmed in Project No. 55566, § 25.195
establishes a generation interconnection cost allowance implementing Senate Bill 1500. Under that
 framework, the transmission service provider (“TSP”) funds a generator’s transmission
interconnection costs up to the applicable allowance and recovers those interconnection costs
up to the allowance through its transmission cost of service; the interconnecting generator bears
only the costs that exceed the allowance. If “interconnection agreements” in § 25.192(e)(6) were
read to include generation interconnection agreements, the provision would prohibit a TSP from
recovering the very § 25.195 allowance the Commission has directed it to recover; an outcome
squarely at odds with § 25.195 and the Senate Bill 1500 framework it implements.

Hunt Energy Network does not believe the Commission intends this result. This rulemaking
implements Senate Bill 6 and is directed at large load. Read in that context, § 25.192(e)(6) is
plainly aimed at large load interconnection agreements under § 25.194 of this title (relating to
Large Load Interconnection Standards) consistent with proposed § 25.252(c)(2)(iii), which
prohibits an allowance for a large load customer’s contribution in aid of construction. A narrow
edit tying § 25.192(e)(6) to § 25.194 would confirm that intent and eliminate any tension with the
generation interconnection allowance.

Hunt Energy Network therefore respectfully proposes the following clarifying revision (proposed
additions underlined):

       “(6) Notwithstanding any other provision of this section, transmission
       interconnection costs associated with large load interconnection agreements under
       § 25.194 of this title (relating to Large Load Interconnection Standards) signed after
       the effective date of this section must not be included in a TSP’s transmission cost
       of service or transmission service rates.”

This edit is intended solely to clarify scope; it does not change the treatment of large load
interconnection costs that Staff proposed, and it preserves the generation interconnection cost
recovery framework established under § 25.195. Hunt Energy Network would welcome any
alternative wording that Staff finds preferable to achieve the same clarification.

Conclusion
Hunt Energy Network again thanks Commission Staff for its work on this proposal and appreciates
the Commission’s consideration of these comments. Hunt Energy Network respectfully requests
that the Commission adopt the clarifying revision to § 25.192(e)(6) described above.
 Respectfully submitted,
HUNT ENERGY NETWORK, LLC

By: ______________________________
Amanda Brown
VP, Energy Markets and Regulatory Strategy
Hunt Energy Network, LLC
abrown2@huntenergy.com
Dated: August 11, 2026
                                  EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
                                      Project No. 58000
                         Comments of Hunt Energy Network, LLC

Hunt Energy Network, LLC appreciates Commission Staff’s work on the proposed rules and offers
a single, narrow clarifying recommendation:

   •   Proposed § 25.192(e)(6) bars recovery of transmission interconnection costs associated
       with “interconnection agreements,” but does not specify large load interconnection
       agreements. As written, the unqualified phrase could be read to include generation
       interconnection agreements executed under § 25.195.

   •   Section 25.195 (implementing Senate Bill 1500 in Project No. 55566) establishes a
       generation interconnection cost allowance that the TSP recovers through its transmission
       cost of service. Reading § 25.192(e)(6) to reach generation interconnection agreements
       would prohibit recovery of that allowance contrary to § 25.195.

   •   Hunt Energy Network recommends clarifying § 25.192(e)(6) to apply to large load
       interconnection agreements under § 25.194, confirming that the provision does not
       disturb the § 25.195 generation interconnection cost allowance.
